title: The achromatic number bound by the harmonic index
source: Baoyindureng Wu and Clive Elphick, “Upper bounds for the achromatic and coloring numbers of a graph”, arXiv:1511.00537 (2015). (https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00537)

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-331690-340121-sol62-20261119-r1/CHECK-331690.md (GPT-6.2 Sol, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For every finite simple graph G with at least one edge, every complete colouring (proper or not) uses at most 2R'(G) colours, where R'(G) is the sum over edges uv of 1/max(d(u), d(v)). Hence the achromatic number, the pseudoachromatic number and the Grundy number are all at most 2R'(G), which proves Wu-Elphick Conjecture 4.1 (and 4.2) for all graphs with an edge. The literal statement "for any graph" fails exactly at nonempty edgeless graphs, where the achromatic number is 1 and R' is 0; Lean proves this exact truth set. The source excludes isolated vertices in its neighbouring results, so the result is a proof of the intended conjecture.
significance.caveat: The literal MathDB statement includes edgeless graphs, where it fails trivially; credit is for the theorem on graphs with an edge (root judgment; user may overrule). Significance modest (review 0.35). Lin and Wang, Discrete Applied Mathematics 371 (2025) 60-64, was read only in the publisher abstract and excerpts: their main theorem excludes both colouring numbers, but the full text was not accessible.
